title: Coefficient and functor package on the proved domains
statement:
Use the coefficient stages $A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, finite-type
separated schemes over the fixed algebraic closure of a finite field, and separated
finite-type morphisms of [def-fix-six-functor-datum].
Pullback, tensor and the two direct images have their proved constructible
domains. At finite stages, internal Hom preserves bounded constructible
finite-Tor complexes in both variables by
[cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom].
General internal-Hom coefficient change is [thm-coef-finite-hom].
Integral internal Hom and exceptional inverse image preserve the
specified bounded constructible category by
[cor-coef-integral-internal-hom], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint];
their field versions are [lem-coef-rational-operations], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].
At finite coefficients the domain remains $D^b_{ctf}$; at integral
and field coefficients it is the specified $D^b_c$.
The sharper dimension-free Hom bound and tensor-dual formulas still
require a site-perfect first
argument. Exceptional adjunction here is on these constructible
categories, without asserting an unrestricted unbounded ambient adjoint.
The following seven clauses collect the preceding results.

1. Finite coefficient-field extension is exact. Compatible finite-stage
functors and transformations descend to the idempotent-complete common-stage
$\Qlb$-category.
1. Compactification comparisons for $Rf_!=R\bar f_*j_!$ are independent
of refinement and satisfy the cocycle condition. For a derived-complete
$\mathcal O_E$-object $K$, put
$K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$. Then
$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\simeq Rf_*K_n,
\qquad
(Rf_!K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\simeq Rf_!K_n.
$$
Between finite quotient rings, both direct-image coefficient comparisons
hold on the bounded finite-Tor domains. For a coherent normalized DVR
tower, the canonical reduction of its derived limit recovers its terms
by [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]; uniform finite-level
bounds supply constructibility of the integral output. No such claim
is made for a tower whose normalization has not been proved.
1. Compact-support composition satisfies
$R(gf)_!\simeq Rg_!Rf_!$, with the identity and associativity equations.
For proper $f$, $Rf_!\simeq Rf_*$. For a closed immersion $i$
with open complement $j$, applying $Rf_!$ to the localization triangle gives
$$
R(fj)_!j^*K\longrightarrow Rf_!K\longrightarrow R(fi)_!i^*K\longrightarrow .
$$
1. In a Cartesian square, $g^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*g'^*$ is an isomorphism
if $f$ is proper or $g$ is smooth, and
$g^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!g'^*$ for arbitrary base change, on the stated
bounded coefficient domains: for $g^*Rf_*$ this means bounded-below
complexes with torsion cohomology at the finite stages, and
$D^b_c$ of the adic (pro-étale) categories at $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, $\Qlb$,
obtained from the finite stages by derived limits and transport. For smooth
base change at the integral and field stages retain compatible finite-reduction
etale-origin witnesses, the admissible-lattice hypotheses of
[sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change] and
[sbc-thm-overline-mathbf-q-ell-coefficient-smooth-base-ch], and their
uniform finite-level constructibility and interval hypotheses whenever the
conclusion is asserted in $D^b_c$. Without those landing hypotheses the
smooth exchange is asserted in the ambient completed category only. At finite
pro-etale coefficients retain the etale-origin domain. No claim is made for
discrete non-torsion coefficients on the small étale site.
1. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$,
the compact-support projection map is an isomorphism:
$$
Rf_!K\otimes^L L\simeq Rf_!(K\otimes^L f^*L).
$$
1. Smooth purity for relative dimension $r$ identifies
$Rf^!L\simeq f^*L(r)[2r]$, with its normalized trace, on the
admissible domains and coefficient stages proved in the purity chapter.
1. For separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ and structure morphisms set
$\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda$ and
$D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$. For
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, the formal Verdier exchange map of
[fix-cor-verdier-exchange] is a natural isomorphism
$$
D_YRf_!M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_*D_XM.
$$
Point biduality and smooth site-perfect biduality are proved independently.
At every finite stage $A=A_{E,n}$, the general anti-equivalence
$D_Y:D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, with
$D_Y^2\simeq\operatorname{id}$, is
[thm-fix-general-biduality]. Its geometric proof also supplies the
finite-stage boundary comparison in
[cor-weil-boundary-duality-discharge].
The coefficient comparisons and uniform bounds are proved separately
in [thm-coef-integral-verdier], [thm-coef-rational-verdier], [thm-coef-qbar-verdier].
They give the same anti-equivalence and evaluation-defined biduality
on $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_c(Y,E)$, and $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$.
On these domains $Rf^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$, with its exceptional adjunction,
by [lem-coef-finite-exceptional], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], [lem-coef-rational-operations].

All comparisons have the coherence and equivariance proved for their
individual clauses. No clause enlarges the domain of another clause.

proof.text: Establish the finite constructible domains before assembling the clauses. Apply the preservation theorem to pullback, tensor and both direct images. Its site-perfect qualification on the dimension-free Hom bound is retained. Apply the finite constructible-Hom corollary to both finite-Tor inputs and then its general evaluation-defined coefficient comparison. Thus this package does not infer site-perfectness from finite Tor amplitude.

For integral inputs use completed pullback and tensor, not discrete non-torsion etale coefficients. The integral preservation lemmas give bounded constructibility of pullback, tensor, ordinary and compact direct images. The integral Hom corollary supplies preservation and the evaluation-defined reduction map for arbitrary bounded constructible first variables. For the field-stage pullback, tensor and direct images, the operation-reduction statement gives their coefficient-passage comparisons. Exact rational transport and the exact common-stage embeddings of step 3 preserve shifts and these constructible object values. The rational operation theorem supplies the internal-Hom identification; the exceptional and duality assertions are assembled in steps 16–17.

Clause (1): finite coefficient-field extension is exact triangulated by the scalar-extension lemma. Given compatible functors and transformations, apply the descent proposition to their unit, associator and shift equations. This produces functors and equations on the common-stage category; its idempotent-complete triangulated structure and exact stage embeddings are supplied by the triangulation theorem.

Clause (2), compactifications: use the canonical proper/open refinement comparisons on the witnessed etale-origin finite domain. The coherence proposition gives identity, transitivity, common-refinement independence and the cocycle. Bounded constructible finite inputs have etale-origin witnesses by the comparison equivalence. For integral and field inputs use the completed and transported comparison statements of the exchange theorem, retaining their finite-reduction, lattice and amplitude domains; its refinement compatibility identifies the comparisons of the chosen compactifications. No comparison on arbitrary unbounded pro-etale complexes is inferred.

Clause (2), coefficient reduction: apply operation reduction to derived-complete integral inputs for both direct images. For finite quotients apply the ordinary direct-image coefficient theorem with B=A_{E,m} and the compact-support comparison on the finite-Tor domain. For a coherent normalized tower apply effectivity: its actual counit reduction recovers M_n. If these terms are constructible with supports in a single finite interval, this recovery plus derived completeness is exactly membership in the integral category. Effectivity alone supplies neither these bounds nor normalization.

source.place: Clause (2), finite reduction and normalized reconstruction

proof.text: Clause (3), composition and proper coincidence: invert the finite composition isomorphism alpha to obtain the displayed direction R(gf)_! to Rg_!Rf_!. Its unit and associativity identities remain the same equations after inversion. The completed and field composition comparisons in the exchange theorem give the same identities on their coefficient domains. For proper f choose the compactification with open factor the identity, so the defining composite is Rf_*; proper coincidence identifies its exchange with the proper exchange. At integral coefficients take the same identity-open compactification at every level. Its terms and quotient-induced transitions are precisely those defining integral Rf_*; hence the compact-support and ordinary-image towers coincide, so their derived limits coincide. The E and Qbar functors are defined by rational and common-stage passage from these functors, which carries this identification to both field stages.

Clause (3), localization: take the all-stage open–closed triangle with its specified counit, unit and connecting map. At finite coefficients apply triangulated Rf_!. At the integral stage choose one compactification c of f and apply the exact R-linear compact-support reduction-tower functor T_f^c to this distinguished triangle. Its evaluations and strict transition maps are exactly Res_n Rf^c_{!,n}(K_n), naturally on morphisms. Apply the exact total derived inverse-limit functor to the resulting triangle in the derived category of towers. By the integral compact-support definition, the resulting functor is Rf_! on these bounded constructible objects, so its three vertices and arrows are the actual integral images. Exact rational transport gives the E-stage image triangle; exact common-stage descent and its triangulation give the Qbar-stage image triangle. Replace Rf_!j_! and Rf_!i_* by R(fj)_! and R(fi)_! using step 6 and proper coincidence for the closed immersion i. This gives the displayed triangle with the transported connecting map. The all-stage triangle and the comparison equivariance retain the stated Weil version. No coherent triangle is inferred from unrelated levelwise choices. A compactification of f exists by [thm-nagata-compactification]: Y is of finite type over k, hence quasi-compact, and separated, hence quasi-separated; X is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem, so the open immersion j is quasi-compact.

Clause (4), proper ordinary base change: use bounded-below torsion proper base change at finite etale coefficients and its witnessed pro-etale version. For integral coefficients use the constructible-complete corollary, for E its raw rational transport, and for Qbar its common-stage theorem. All schemes in the datum are finite type over k, so the noetherian, finite-dimensional and bounded-relative-dimension hypotheses of these statements apply; the coefficient residue orders are invertible since ell differs from p. Use the specified completed exchange at the integral stage, not the exchange for discrete non-torsion small-etale modules. The finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem applies to Spec k (a field has only the ideals 0 and k), and finite dimension is the finite-type dimension lemma. Finite type gives quasi-compactness; separatedness gives quasi-separatedness because the diagonal is a closed immersion. The uniform fibre-dimension lemma bounds ordinary fibres, and field-extension dimension invariance applied to a finite affine cover of each fibre gives the same bound for geometric fibres, including empty fibres. The proper-base-change stability lemma makes f' proper, as required by the completed and rational proper-base-change statements.

Clause (4), smooth ordinary base change: relabel the smooth-base-change square so its smooth f is the present g, its direct-image g is the present f, its input T is the present X and its output X is the present Y'. The finite etale theorem applies to bounded-below torsion inputs because the coefficient orders are invertible; the finite pro-etale theorem applies to bounded constructible inputs with their etale models. At O_E apply the completed theorem with compatible finite-reduction etale witnesses. At E use a specified admissible lattice; at Qbar use admissible common-stage representatives stable under finite overfields. These yield ambient completed isomorphisms. Retain the explicit uniform finite-level constructibility and interval bounds for a D^b_c conclusion; in particular the Qbar theorem by itself asserts no constructible landing. The exchange-identification statement ensures these are the maps in this package. The finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem applies to Spec k (a field has only the ideals 0 and k), and finite dimension is the finite-type dimension lemma. Finite type gives quasi-compactness; separatedness gives quasi-separatedness because the diagonal is a closed immersion.

source.place: Clause (4), smooth ordinary base change; domain clarification

proof.text: Clause (4), compact supports: use the finite torsion compact-support theorem and its witnessed finite pro-etale version for arbitrary base change. At integral coefficients apply the completed compact-support theorem to the compatible etale-origin reductions; at E apply its raw rational transport and at Qbar the descended exchange theorem. The isomorphism is on precisely the coefficient categories in those statements; no smoothness of the base-change map is needed. The finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem applies to Spec k (a field has only the ideals 0 and k), and finite dimension is the finite-type dimension lemma. Finite type gives quasi-compactness; separatedness gives quasi-separatedness because the diagonal is a closed immersion. The compactification required by the finite torsion and completed compact-support theorems exists by [thm-nagata-compactification], since Y is quasi-compact and separated (hence quasi-separated); its open immersion is quasi-compact because X is Noetherian.

Clause (5) is the projection theorem applied to the given bounded constructible K and finite-Tor L. Its displayed map has the same direction as the map in this package. Its theorem includes naturality and the composition, compactification, reduction, scalar-extension and proper-coincidence comparisons on exactly these domains.

Clause (6): invert the finite smooth-purity map gamma to obtain Rf^!L isomorphic to f^*L(r)[2r]. For integral inputs apply the adic reconstruction theorem to the normalized compatible finite family; for rational and Qbar inputs use the specified normalized integral lattice and purity transport. The smooth trace is the exceptional counit read through gamma, as specified in the smooth-trace definition. Reduction compatibility includes this trace, so the normalization and the comparison are retained. This uses the lecture-notes diagonal/deformation route already represented by the finite purity theorem.

Clause (7), exchange: apply the unconditional constructible Verdier-exchange theorem with the structure morphisms of X and Y. It states the canonical natural map D_Y Rf_!M to Rf_*D_XM for every finite-Tor constructible M, including its coefficient and shift comparisons. This is the constructible version of the formal exchange named in the statement; it does not require the stronger unrestricted ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility of the older interface.

Clause (7), independent point and perfect cases: apply the coefficient Frobenius lemma using derived evaluation at O_E, and ordinary exact duality at the finite and field stages. For a smooth pure-dimensional scheme and a site-perfect input, use the perfect-duality theorem: its orientation-induced formula identifies Verdier biduality with coefficient-perfect biduality. This supplies these special cases without deriving the general geometric statement from a site-perfect hypothesis.

Clause (7), general finite coefficients: apply geometric biduality directly on D^b_ctf at A_{E,n}, where it asserts exact anti-equivalence and the natural evaluation biduality isomorphism. Apply the boundary-discharge corollary for the closed immersions of its locally closed pieces. The latter is a consequence available after geometric duality, not an extra hypothesis used to prove that duality.

source.place: Clause (7), geometric biduality and boundary comparison

proof.text: Clause (7), integral and field coefficients: apply integral Verdier duality, which includes the equality of the integral bounded constructible and uniform finite-Tor domains, uniform dimension-dependent output bounds, evaluation-defined finite reductions and evaluation biduality. Rational Verdier duality gives the E-linear anti-equivalence by rationalizing those maps. Qbar Verdier duality descends these exact anti-equivalences, evaluations and double-dual maps through finite scalar extension and retracts. Thus the claimed evaluation-defined bidualities are the actual coefficient-passage maps.

The exceptional formula and adjunction in clause (7) are assembled with their coefficient domains. For the fixed compactification c=(j,p), p is proper and therefore finite type; since Y is finite type over k, so is its source. The finite-type dimension lemma supplies the nonnegative dimension bound required by the class-relative adjunction theorem (use zero for an empty compactification). At finite stages use the class-relative exceptional adjunction on bounded constructible objects together with the finite formula Rf^!=D_Xf^*D_Y and its quotient cocycle, units and counits. At O_E the integral adjoint theorem gives preservation, the same completed-pullback formula and the reduction-identified adjunction. At E use the rational operation theorem, and at Qbar use the descended constructible adjunction. None of these steps asserts an adjoint on arbitrary unbounded pro-etale objects. The compactification c exists by [thm-nagata-compactification], Y being quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated.

Apply the coherence theorem to precisely the proved comparison maps used above. Its identity, composition, exchange and projection equations, coefficient comparisons and field Weil equivariance give the final sentence. This only collects each established compatibility: it adds no arbitrary-base-change commutation for Verdier duality and does not enlarge any domain.

proof_origin.place: Opening domain paragraph; clauses (1)–(7); final coherence sentence. Expanded terminal assembly with explicit coefficient domains and current constructible interfaces.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q108-975471fd7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the full item (statement and 18 steps), the main-20261015 and master blueprint statement and proof (the statement text is the same in both), the unit and chapter records, and the current statements of all 66 cited nodes plus the 2 statement-only dependencies. No cycle: the transitive closure from every dependency never reaches the item. All off-route citations are among the six declared tool_uses, and I accept them: lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change and the five sbc-thm-* nodes, which are the coefficient-stage forms of the on-route smooth-base-change unit. No SGA citation; purity follows the lecture-notes route. Checks by step: (3) descent needs the unit, associator and shift equations, which the step requires. (5) normalized effectivity is kept separate from the uniform bounds. (6) inverting alpha gives the displayed direction, and with c=(id,f) the integral compact-support and ordinary towers are equal. (7) localization uses the exact tower functor T_f^c and the exact total derived limit, so no triangle is built from unrelated levelwise choices. (8) Noetherian, finite-dimension, fibre-bound, geometric-fibre and f'-proper hypotheses are each cited; empty fibres are allowed. (9) the smooth-base-change relabelling (sbc f = g, sbc g = f, T = X, sbc X = Y') and the map direction match. (13) fix-cor-verdier-exchange assumes ambient admissibility, which fails in general; thm-sf-verdier-exchange is unconditional and builds the same composite from the same composition mate (written in the opposite direction there). (14) O_E uses derived evaluation. (17) the dimension bound for the compactification is supplied. Clause (4) differs from the blueprint by a typing qualification for smooth base change at O_E, E and Qbar. It is true and identical to the merged fix-lem-exchanges clause 3. For D^b_c inputs the witnesses and lattice it asks for are automatic: witnesses are part of the pbc D^b_c definition, and K itself with the identity is a lattice. Landing in D^b_c follows from lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible, already used in step 2. No citer uses integral or field smooth base change from the package. So I accept it as a reported clarification, not a source error. FIX, C1: steps 7, 10 and 17 choose a compactification, and thm-cbc-finite-torsion and thm-cbc-complete-proetale require one, but no step proved that one exists. I added thm-nagata-compactification (on route): Y is quasi-compact (finite type over k) and quasi-separated (separated), and j is quasi-compact because X is Noetherian (step 7 also cites lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian). proof_deps updated; nothing else changed. Small cases checked: X empty, K=0, f=id, n=1, m=n, g=id, relative dimension 0, the A^1 origin for the site-perfect bound, and a torsion module at an O_E point. Minor: the report says source.document was moved to main-20261015, but it still points to master; the statement is the same in both, so I left it.
